# nuthatch nest on arbitrum-one

A self-hosted blockchain index. Query it locally; there is no third-party API.

## Contracts
- `gns` = 0xec9A7fb6CbC2E41926127929c2dcE6e9c5D33Bec

## Tables (one per contract event)
- `gns__legacy_subgraph_claimed` - LegacySubgraphClaimed(address,uint256) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, graphAccount, subgraphNumber)
- `gns__set_default_name` - SetDefaultName(address,uint256,bytes32,string) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, graphAccount, nameSystem, nameIdentifier, name)
- `gns__subgraph_deprecated` - SubgraphDeprecated(uint256,uint256) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, subgraphID, withdrawableGRT)
- `gns__subgraph_metadata_updated` - SubgraphMetadataUpdated(uint256,bytes32) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, subgraphID, subgraphMetadata)
- `gns__subgraph_published` - SubgraphPublished(uint256,bytes32,uint32) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, subgraphID, subgraphDeploymentID, reserveRatio)
- `gns__subgraph_received_from_l1` - SubgraphReceivedFromL1(uint256,uint256,address,uint256) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, _l1SubgraphID, _l2SubgraphID, _owner, _tokens)
- `gns__subgraph_upgraded` - SubgraphUpgraded(uint256,uint256,uint256,bytes32) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, subgraphID, vSignalCreated, tokensSignalled, subgraphDeploymentID)
- `gns__subgraph_version_updated` - SubgraphVersionUpdated(uint256,bytes32,bytes32) (block_number, block_hash, block_timestamp, tx_hash, log_index, address, _seq, subgraphID, subgraphDeploymentID, versionMetadata)

## Live HTTP API (run `nuthatch dev`)
- `GET /`                    index status
- `GET /tables`              every table with its columns
- `GET /table/{name}?limit=N` recent rows of one table (hot + sealed)
- `GET /entity/{id}`         one row by id (`{block:012}-{logindex:06}`)
- `GET /sql?q=SELECT...`     read-only SQL; each table is a view named `{alias}__{event}`
- `GET /balances?limit=N`    top holder balances (when an ERC-20 Transfer table is present)
- `GET /balance/{address}`   one address's derived balance

## MCP (for coding agents)
Run `nuthatch mcp` (stdio) to expose tools: status, schema, tables, table, sql, entity,
balance, top_balances. Fully offline against the local instance; nothing phones home.
